plan: This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction with independent private values. In such auctions, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do, since the payment depends on the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Overbidding risks paying more than the item's worth to me if I win against a high second bid; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly my private value of $6, ensuring I only win when profitable and pay a fair price when I do.

This is a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid). In second-price auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid one's true value, regardless of beliefs about opponents' strategies. Bidding truthfully ensures I win exactly when it's profitable (value > price paid) and never overpay. Since my value is $40, I should bid $40.

In a second-price (Vickrey) auction with independent private values, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. This holds because deviating from truthful bidding either loses value when winning or forgoes profitable wins. Since my value is $28, I will bid exactly that amount, ensuring optimal expected profit regardless of competitors' behavior.
